messages:
jess: heads up — customer `evokeai` reported a spike of 504/5xx on hosted inference when onboarding 1200 concurrent sessions around 09:42 UTC. Gateway timeouts and many short-lived 502s mixed in.

sre-jen: saw alerts — queue depth for tenant=evokeai jumped, scaler didn't catch up. KEDA log shows scaledobject events: 'scale suppressed by external metric timeout' and scheduler showing pod pending due to nodeAffinity scoring.

ryan: can you paste the exact errors? any auth/billing 403s?

jess: no 403s. Main symptom: front-gateway 504s, runtime returned 502s intermittently. Example from gateway logs: `upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream`.

maria: grabbing k8s events now. Found a flurry of pod pulls -> Eviction/backoff on node pool autoscaler: `PodFitsHostPorts` and custom affinity to GPU-pools caused pods to be funneled to a single AZ, saturating nodepool and throttling scheduler.

sre-jen: that explains slow warmups. Also KEDA poll interval for the metric was 30s and cooldown 120s — during the spike it never reached the target since many pods were Pending.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4592. Priority: P1 (customer-facing timeouts). Pager duty notified.

ryan: short mitigation: temporarily remove strict nodeAffinity so pods can schedule across AZs and trigger burst nodes. Also shorten KEDA polling/cooldown for that scaler.

jess: confirmed — I patched the deployment annotation to relax affinity (added toleration to allow non-GPU hot nodes) and increased scaledobject minReplicas from 2 to 10. Patch command I ran: ```kubectl -n prod patch scaledobject evokeai-scaledobj --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicaCount","value":10}]'```

maria: after patch gateway 504 rate dropped from 18% -> 3% in 6 minutes. Some pods still initializing (model init time ~18s) causing a few 502s.

alex: reproducible repro steps documented: 1) simulate tenant burst with siege load hitting /v1/generate with 1k concurrent connections 2) watch keda metrics and `kubectl get pods -o wide` to observe Pending pods 3) check scheduler events for affinity failures.

sre-jen: root causes summary: (a) overly strict nodeAffinity + small GPU AZ footprint created scheduling hot spot, (b) KEDA config cooldown + poll intervals too conservative for short bursts, (c) model warmup latency (no prewarm for this model) amplified customer timeouts.

ryan: next-actions — create infra ticket to relax affinity defaults for tenant onboarding and add recommendation to provisioning docs; tweak KEDA defaults for high-concurrency tenants; add optional prewarm hook for heavy models. I'll own the infra ticket.

jess: support reply to customer: "We've applied emergency scheduler relaxation and scaled the service — you should see reduced errors. We're following up with permanent config changes and a postmortem." Sent.


deploy-bot: deploy 2026-07-21T09:55:00Z: rolled config patch to evokeai-scaledobj (minReplicas=10) by jess.

maria: filing postmortem/retro, will attach logs and the kube repro steps. assigning action items to infra and runtime teams.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-4592 status: Mitigated -> Monitoring.

jess: closing thread — will add playbook snippet for future: 1) check affinity events, 2) relax nodeAffinity, 3) bump minReplicas, 4) shorten KEDA poll/cooldown, 5) apply prewarm policy. Thanks all :thumbsup:
